title: Urine collection, analysis window & preservatives
guide: Second morning sample by midstream technique; analyse within 2–4 h at room temperature and check pH immediately; formaldehyde or glutaraldehyde as preservatives, 2–8°C for up to 12 h; no strenuous exercise for 72 h, no collection during menses, and in catheterised patients always fresh urine — never from the urobag.

title: Appearance: colour table & its drug causes
guide: Light yellow is normal and pale/white means high water intake; pink = desferrioxamine or beetroot; imipenem + cilastatin darkens on standing; triamterene (ENaC blocker) greens, nitrofurantoin browns, rifampicin and entacapone (COMT inhibitor) orange.

title: Odour table: metabolic diseases and their smells
guide: Pungent = infection until proven otherwise (bacterial ammonia); musty/mousy PKU; curry/maple syrup MSUD; sweaty feet isovaleric acidemia or glutaric aciduria II; cabbage-like and rancid butter both = tyrosinemia type I; cat urine MCD; acid smell MMA; fish trimethylaminuria; sulfurous cystinuria; sweet beta-ketothiolase deficiency; swimming pool hawkinsinuria.

title: Other properties, acidification & concentration
guide: Urine pH 4–4.5, SG 1.020–1.040, osmolality 800–900 against blood 7.35–7.40 / 1.010 / 285–290. α-Intercalated cells of the CCD secrete H+ (NH4+ = non-titratable major acid, H2PO4− = titratable); concentration needs ADH, urea-driven medullary osmolality and vasa recta. pH >5.5 × 3 days with normal RFT = type-1 RTA; SG <1.005 with osmolality <300 = DI; isosthenuria = ATN/CTID.

title: High-coloured urine: causes & the dipstick–spin–biopsy approach
guide: 90% urological (carcinoma bladder m/c), 9% nephrological, 1% hematological (intravascular hemolysis). Dipstick positive → spin at 1600 rpm × 5 min: clear supernatant = RBCs (glomerular if ≥40% dysmorphic, ≥5% acanthocytes or a single RBC cast with proteinuria → biopsy → mesangial disease/IgA; else radiological), coloured supernatant left 3–6 h fades with myoglobin and stays with haemoglobin.

title: RBC morphology & the dipstick parameter table
guide: Panel A (urological) = crenated, isomorphic; panels B and C (nephrological) = dysmorphic and acanthocyte 'mickey mouse' cells. Leukocytes and nitrites share one UTI cell (high specificity, poor sensitivity), urobilinogen = extravascular hemolysis, glucose = proximal RTA (euglycemic glycosuria) and SGLT2 inhibitors (euglycemic ketosis); protein/pH/blood/SG/ketones/bilirubin carry a dash. Concentrated urine, high density, proteinuria, glucosuria, cephalothin, tetracycline, cephalexin and tobramycin disturb the leukocyte pad.

title: Proteinuria: uromodulin, cut-offs, albumin & tests
guide: Uromodulin (Tamm-Horsfall) is 70–80 mg/day from the thick ascending limb, the commonest urinary protein and the cast matrix. <150 normal; 150–500 functional (stress, anxiety, menses, protein supplements); >500 significant, >300 in pregnancy. Albumin: <30 normal, 30–300 microalbuminuria (a vascular-integrity marker needing evaluation), >300 albuminuria; albumin → tubular injury → inflammation → TGF-β → fibrosis. Four tests; the dipstick is qualitative, only lights up near 800 mg, sees albumin only, and must be supplemented.

title: Microscopy: cells, Maltese cross & cast formation
guide: RBC < WBC < epithelial cell. Phase contrast shows monomorphic cells in urological bleeding; tubular epithelial cells have granular cytoplasm and a lobulated nucleus; oval fat bodies show the Maltese cross — in blood with babesiosis, in kidney with Fabry's, ADPKD, acute/chronic interstitial nephritis and prerenal azotemia. Casts form in the DCT; hyaline = normal or kidney disease, granular = kidney disease.

title: Casts and their clinical associations
guide: Pigment fine granular = pigment nephropathy (hemolysis, rhabdomyolysis); RBC = glomerular hematuria; WBC = acute pyelonephritis, PSGN, ATN/AIN; tubular epithelial (muddy brown) = most specific for ATN/AIN; broad + waxy = CKD; fatty = lipiduria of nephrotic syndrome and Fabry's; eosinophil = ATN/AIN; fractured (on biopsy) = myeloma.

title: Urinary crystals, shapes and panels
guide: A uric acid rhomboid; B calcium oxalate dihydrate bipyramidal/envelope; C monohydrate dumb-bell; D calcium phosphate star-shaped in alkaline urine; E struvite (MgNH4PO4) coffin-lid; F cholesterol (no shape given); G hexagonal cystine; plus the broom-brush amoxicillin crystals.
